profile.entities: Max Healthcare Institute Ltd; Kalinga Hospital Ltd (Acquired)
profile.subseg: Tertiary Care Hospitals; Oncology; Day Care; Diagnostics (Max Lab); Home Healthcare (Max@Home); International Patients
profile.themes: Brownfield Capacity Ramp-up; Oncology Drug Policy Disruption (CGHS/ECHS); Eastern India Entry; Greenfield Expansion (Gurgaon/Lucknow)

bull_bear.body: Debt reduction priority (Net debt down to INR 1,908cr from INR 2,166cr); Dividend paid INR 146cr in FY26; M&A active (Kalinga Hospital acquisition); Reinvestment in brownfield/greenfield projects to capture market share in North/East India.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory Pricing: CGHS/ECHS mandate for 30% discount on chemo drugs causing permanent revenue mix shift and potential patient attrition to unorganized sector; Execution Risk: Delays in Gurgaon/Lucknow commissioning due to labor shortages (LPG crisis/elections); Talent Inflation: Rising doctor costs in competitive micro-markets; ALOS Volatility: Temporary inefficiencies during phased bed rollouts.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on volume growth and capacity utilization; Pragmatic on oncology drug issue (viewed as permanent structural shift, not temporary); Aggressive on expansion (Lucknow/Gurgaon) despite macro headwinds; Emphasized 'cluster approach' to mitigate doctor talent bottlenecks.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Oncology drug discontinuation is industry-wide but impacts Max disproportionately due to high institutional mix; Management views the exit of these drugs as margin-accretive long-term despite top-line hit (exiting 'perverse' margins); Kalinga Hospital was acquired profitably (INR 10cr annual EBITDA), avoiding typical startup losses; ALOS increase is a tactical artifact of opening beds only when demand exists, not clinical inefficiency.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Hospitals: 75%+ occupancy, ARPOB INR 77,900; Oncology share dropped to 21% (vs 26% YoY) due to CGHS drug pricing policy; International Patients: INR 227cr (+12% YoY, 9% of hospital rev); Max@Home: INR 73cr (+30% YoY); Max Lab: INR 52cr (+14% YoY). Digital revenue 31% of total.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin compressed 40bps YoY to 26.8% primarily due to exit of low-margin (16%) but high-revenue oncology drugs for institutional patients; Doctor costs elevated due to pre-hiring for new capacities (INR 435cr in Q4), expected to normalize with operating leverage; CGHS rate revision benefit (INR 140cr annualized net) partially offset drug loss, with INR 30-40cr yet to flow.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Mid-to-high single digits organic + capacity additions; Margin: Expect recovery as new beds ramp (operating leverage), oncology share to stabilize at 21-22%; Order Inflow: Strong demand in Lucknow/Delhi NCR; Capex: INR 1,400cr approved for Lucknow greenfield; Commissioning: Gurgaon (500 beds) by end-FY27, Mohali/Nagpur by FY28.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion Pipeline: 500 beds Gurgaon (FY27); 700 beds Lucknow Greenfield (Board approved INR 1,400cr); 400 beds Mohali (FY28); 260 beds Dwarka (24 months); 200 beds Vaishali (pending approval); 400 beds Patparganj (FY29). Total upcoming capacity ~2,500+ beds over 3-4 years.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Eastern India entry via Kalinga Hospital (Bhubaneswar, 250 beds, already profitable); Lucknow cluster strategy (Gomti Nagar expansion + 700-bed Shaheed Path greenfield); Phased brownfield ramp-up in Delhi/Mumbai/Punjab yielding operating leverage as occupancy stabilizes near 80%.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Max Healthcare delivered steady 10% revenue growth in Q4FY26 driven by volume (OBDs +8%), but faced a structural margin headwind from discontinuing low-margin institutional oncology drugs (-5% oncology share). The strategic pivot involves absorbing this permanent revenue mix shift while aggressively ramping 20% new brownfield capacity and entering Eastern India via the profitable Kalinga acquisition, positioning FY27 for operating leverage as new beds fill.

open.item: Phase-II of the Nanavati-Max, Mumbai expansion (an additional 271 beds) has on-ground construction activities scheduled to commence in FY2026-27.

New 130-bed built-to-suit hospital near existing Max Dehradun, focused on advanced oncology including radiation therapy, with ~Rs.170-200 Crore of Company investment, expected to be commissioned by FY2028-29.
~450-bed super speciality hospital in Pune (Yerawada Properties acquisition) at an estimated project cost of ~Rs.1,020 Crore, expected to be commissioned within the next 4 years.
Received Board approval to add a 260-bed brownfield tower at Max Dwarka, Delhi.
Company plans to develop a 712-bed greenfield hospital on its 5-acre land parcel at Shaheed Path, Lucknow, to address rising demand for specialised healthcare in an underserved region.
Overall expansion pipeline has the potential to add over 8,300 beds, including approximately 4,000 beds over the next three to four years.

Board approved (May 21, 2026) construction of Phase-I of Max Super Speciality Hospital, Shaheed Path, Lucknow — ~712 census beds — at a total construction & equipment cost of ~Rs.1,400 Crore (blended cost per bed ~Rs.1.97 Crore, excluding land).

Crosslay Remedies Limited acquired a ~1-acre land parcel adjoining Max Super Speciality Hospital, Vaishali for ~Rs.120 Crore, expected to facilitate ~200 additional beds at the site over the next 2-3 years.
Board approved (May 20, 2025) expansion of Max Super Speciality Hospital, Nagpur by ~100 beds (from existing 200 beds) via two additional floors, to be added over the next 2-3 years.

Board approved (February 5, 2026) an amendment to the Services Agreement with Muthoot Hospitals Private Limited to extend the Dwarka hospital arrangement to ~260 additional beds proposed to be developed at the same site.
Max Smart, Saket 400-bed brownfield tower being operationalised in phases; 156 beds already handed over, balance expected to be commissioned over the next quarter.
Received Board approval for a 712-bed greenfield hospital at Shaheed Path, Lucknow.
Company is planning development of a 400-bed asset-light hospital in Zirakpur to strengthen its presence in the Tricity region.
Nanavati-Max, Mumbai Phase II — an additional 271-bed brownfield tower — is expected to commence on-ground work upon full commissioning of Phase I (280-bed tower).
Overall pipeline has the potential to add over 8,300 beds, including approximately 4,000 beds over the next three to four years.
Company intends to maintain net debt-to-EBITDA at not more than 2.5x to preserve balance sheet strength while funding growth.
Multiple projects across Lucknow, Nagpur, Zirakpur, Pitampura, Dwarka, Vaishali, Dehradun, Thane and Pune are shaping the next phase of network growth.
Executed agreements to expand geographical footprint in Dehradun (130 beds), Pune (450 beds) and Bhubaneswar (250 beds).
Long-term ambition of nearly doubling bed capacity over the next five years, guided by disciplined capital allocation and phased execution.
Gurugram facility is progressing steadily and is expected to become operational in 2026.

drhp.business: Max Healthcare Institute Limited operates a network of 21 healthcare facilities across 11 cities in India with over 6,000 beds, delivering tertiary and quaternary care across specialities including oncology, cardiac sciences, neurosciences, orthopaedics, renal sciences and organ transplantation. Beyond hospitals, the Company extends its care ecosystem through Max Lab (pathology and diagnostics) and Max@Home (home healthcare and wellness services), and serves international patients through Patient Assistance Centres across multiple countries.
